title: ‘GTA VI’ Is a Perfect Game. Rushing Through It Would Be a Mistake
gist: WIRED's early-hours impression of Grand Theft Auto VI says the game has lived up to 13 years of hype with near-universally perfect reviews, trading the franchise's arcade style for a slower, Red Dead Redemption 2-like deliberateness in a vast, photorealistic Leonida. Built over 13 years for around a billion dollars by Rockstar and Take-Two, it is framed as likely the last grand blockbuster made without generative AI.

insights.claim: Grand Theft Auto VI launched to near-universally perfect review scores and, in WIRED's view, has surpassed 13 years of hype to become one of the very best games as well as the biggest.
insights.speaker: Boone Ashworth
insights.so_what: Strong reviews support long-tail sales and engagement for Take-Two's flagship title.
insights.locator: The biggest video game ever has turned out

insights.claim: Rockstar and parent company Take-Two spent around a billion dollars and 13 years developing GTA VI, delaying it multiple times to polish it.
insights.speaker: Boone Ashworth
insights.so_what: A roughly $1 billion budget sets the bar for AAA development cost and the revenue GTA VI must earn for Take-Two.
insights.locator: If you’ve followed the GTA VI saga

insights.claim: WIRED argues GTA VI is likely to be the pinnacle of this era of video games and the final grand blockbuster made without generative AI.
insights.speaker: Boone Ashworth
insights.so_what: Signals expectation that future AAA production will lean on generative AI, which could reshape game-development costs and labor.
insights.quote: the final grand blockbuster achieved without the use of generative AI.
insights.locator: There is massive hype, and at this point

insights.claim: GTA VI departs from the franchise's high-octane arcade style toward a slower, more deliberate play style resembling Red Dead Redemption 2, with heavier vehicles, deeper characters, a more reactive world and chores such as limited carried inventory and waiting for car repairs.
insights.speaker: Boone Ashworth
insights.so_what: A design shift toward immersion and slower pacing may extend player engagement time but risks alienating fans seeking arcade action.
insights.locator: I’ve spent a few hours in the game

insights.claim: GTA VI's Leonida, a mirror version of Miami, Florida, is vast and fully detailed, with driving scenes photorealistic enough to resemble real dash-cam footage.
insights.speaker: Boone Ashworth
insights.so_what: Sets a new graphical and world-building benchmark that competitors will be measured against.
insights.locator: There is just so much Leonida
